title: CheckMyCoach: Controlled Evaluation of LLM Correction Strategies
oneLiner: A provenance-preserving framework for comparing evidence-based correction strategies on a fixed corpus.
keyTakeaways: The v2.2 package compares Original, Generic, Generic plus a frozen Oracle Failure Specification, and the selectively routed CheckMyCoach pipeline on 40 constructed fitness-advice cases.
Generic and Generic+Oracle each removed the prespecified targeted failure in 36/40 cases, with identical case-level targeted-removal outcomes in this single execution.
CheckMyCoach routed 15/40 cases to correction. All 15 attempted M3 calls returned a correction; 12 passed M4 and removed the targeted failure, yielding 12/40 end-to-end targeted-failure removal.

No CheckMyCoach output passed every deterministic target-and-retention check. The experiment does not establish superiority, validated detection, equivalence, human benefit, or cross-domain generalization.
hciRelevance: Provides a controlled way to separate routing coverage, correction execution, validator acceptance, targeted-failure removal, and information retention before testing effects on human reliance.

faq.q: Did the oracle failure specification improve correction?
faq.a: Not in this single 40-case execution: Generic and Generic+Oracle had identical targeted-removal decisions. This is not an equivalence or non-inferiority result and does not prove that oracle information has no value.

faq.q: How did the full CheckMyCoach pipeline perform?
faq.a: M1 routed 15/40 constructed failures to M3. Twelve delivered outputs removed the targeted failure, so the end-to-end result was 12/40. The other 25 cases were not API failures; they never reached M3.

faq.q: Has the evaluation been human validated?
faq.a: No. Outcomes are deterministic proxy checks on one fixed constructed corpus. No usability, trust, safety, or human-validity claim is made.
